title: Anisotropic Ion Migration and Electronic Conduction in van der Waals Ferroelectric CuInP2S6

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: vdW electronic devices need controlled ionic manipulation in layered ferroelectric/dielectric materials. Whether Cu ion migration in CIPS follows distinct in-plane and out-of-plane paths is not directly resolved at the nanoscale.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/gap), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/method), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/forming), n7 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The flake surface is a network of ferroelectric CIPS lamellae embedded in a paraelectric IPS matrix. Poling leaves a Cu-rich zone in the biased CIPS region.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The CIPS phase conducts under a -3 V tip bias while the surrounding IPS phase stays insulating. CIPS conductivity rises with how long the material is held in the tip field (slower scan, slower ramp, longer hold).
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (PRP/value), n10 (PRP/value), n11 (MEC/pathway), n14 (PRP/behavior_class), n15 (MEC/identification). Premises: In CIPS the Cu+ occupies three sites: Cu1 quasi-trigonal with up/down states, Cu2 octahedral, and Cu3 almost tetrahedral, penetrating the vdW gap; Conductivity that grows with slower scanning or more cycles is a known activation signature of ionic conductors such as KTiOPO4; Reported activation energies are higher out-of-plane than in-plane: Ea = 0.85/0.23 eV and EA = 1.16/0.55 eV (OOP/IP), with EA = Ea + Ec

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Nanoscale ionic conduction of the CIPS flake on a flexible PMMA/PEN substrate is switched and amplified electrically at room temperature
states.detail: Absorbed: n16 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: CIPS has Tc = 310 K and its ionic conductivity onsets near 250 K, so Cu hopping is thermally activated at room temperature

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Cu ion migration and the resulting conduction in vdW ferroelectric CIPS are anisotropic, with the easier in-plane path, guiding vdW ionic-electronic device design

nodes.title: evidence, F4, F6
nodes.head: Current profiles across the same box reach -1.6 pA at 2 um/s and about -110 pA at 0.5 um/s, a roughly 70-fold increase at the slower scan. At a fixed -4 V the CIPS current grows steadily from 0 to about -700 pA over 300 s while the IPS current stays at 0.
nodes.solves: CIPS conductivity rises with how long the material is held in the tip field (slower scan, slower ramp, longer hold)
nodes.note: linked text states about 60-fold; the plotted minima give about 70-fold
nodes.detail: o5: Current profiles across the same box reach -1.6 pA at 2 um/s and about -110 pA at 0.5 um/s, a roughly 70-fold increase at the slower scan; o8: At a fixed -4 V the CIPS current grows steadily from 0 to about -700 pA over 300 s while the IPS current stays at 0; o18: The bias-on current restarts higher at each successive cycle, reaching about -230 pA by 800 s

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: The first bias-on maximum current is comparable in the three runs: -11, -14 and -17 pA. With -8 V on / 30 s off cycling the current falls to zero at every bias-off and recovers as soon as the bias returns
nodes.solves: Conduction in the CIPS phase is dominantly ionic, carried by Cu+ migration, not purely electronic
nodes.detail: o13: The first bias-on maximum current is comparable in the three runs: -11, -14 and -17 pA; o14: With -8 V on / 30 s off cycling the current falls to zero at every bias-off and recovers as soon as the bias returns

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: In the 230-330 s window the bias-on current falls in two segments: a steep drop to about -12 pA labelled Stage I, then a shallower linear fall to -50 pA labelled Stage II. With a 1 s bias-off the steep initial segment is absent and the current falls in one slope, unlike the 30 s bias-off run
nodes.solves: Two Cu+ paths operate: fast in-plane intralayer hopping (stage I) and slower out-of-plane interlayer hopping across the vdW gap (stage II)
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: at the printed scale the first seconds of each cycle are only a few pixels; the single-slope reading is weaker than the two-stage reading in F6g
